title: Live imaging of Drosophila melanogaster neural stem cells with photo-ablated centrosomes
author: Thomas, Giet
materials: Rabbit polyclonal anti-phospho Histone H3 antibodies

steps.title: Prepare incubation chamber
steps.instruction: Assemble a stainless‑steel slide (76 mm × 26 mm × 1 mm) with a 40 × 22 mm coverslip glued using VALAP (1/3 Vaseline, 1/3 Lanolin, 1/3 Paraffin) and let it harden.

substeps.instruction: Place the slide upside down on a dry‑bath incubator at 70 °C.
Apply a small amount of melted VALAP near the central well with a spatula.
Place the coverslip on the VALAP and allow capillary diffusion.
Return the chamber to 18 °C–22 °C to harden the VALAP.
The central well is a 16 mm diameter (0.8 mm high) cavity containing a centered 5 mm well (0.2 mm high).
Store coverslips in 95 % ethanol; avoid VALAP spilling into the well.

steps.title: Dissect larval brain
steps.instruction: Wash larvae, isolate brains, and keep them in pre‑warmed culture medium.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑heat culture medium to 25 °C and centrifuge at × g for 1 min to remove debris.
Wash larvae three times in PBS and transfer them to 200 µL of the culture medium.
Under a binocular, use fine tweezers to remove the brain and surrounding tissues.
Separate the brain from salivary glands and any remaining tissue.

steps.title: Mount brain in chamber
steps.instruction: Transfer the dissected brain to the incubation chamber, cover with mineral oil, and gently remove excess medium.

substeps.instruction: Cut the tip of a 200 µL Eppendorf pipette with a razor blade.
Aspirate the brain with the tip containing 50 µL of culture medium and place it in the central well of the chamber.
Immediately add 200 µL of mineral oil on top of the brain.
Using a fine homemade glass capillary, aspirate excess culture medium through the oil layer until the brain lobes just begin to flatten (monitor under the binocular).

steps.title: Verify centrosome ablation (immunostaining)
steps.instruction: Fix the photo‑ablated brain and stain for centrosomal markers.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate the brain with a Pasteur pipette containing 50 µL of culture medium.
Transfer the brain to 1 mL of fresh fixative solution (Bonaccorsi et al., 2011).
Invert the tube three times and incubate at 25 °C for 20 min.
Allow the sample to sink by capillarity and discard the fixative.
Wash the fixed brain three times for 10 min each on a rotating wheel in 1 mL PBST.
Proceed with immunofluorescence using rabbit anti‑Cnn, rat anti‑tubulin, and mouse anti‑phospho‑Histone H3 (Ser10) antibodies.

steps.title: Analyze images and plot data
steps.instruction: Measure daughter cell sizes, create movies, and perform statistical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Open time‑lapse recordings in Fiji (ImageJ).
Visualize NSC and GMC outlines with the PH‑PLCδ‑GFP plasma‑membrane marker.
Measure the diameter of each newborn NSC and GMC after cytokinesis using the line tool; take at least two measurements per cell and calculate the mean.
Generate movies of control and photo‑ablated NSCs in Fiji.
Plot the diameter data and run statistical tests in Prism.
Select representative time‑lapse frames for figures or export videos.

steps.title: Clean chamber after imaging
steps.instruction: Remove residual mounting medium and reuse the stainless‑steel slide.

substeps.instruction: Wipe off remaining mounting medium.
Heat the slide upside down on a 70 °C heating block.
Carefully remove the coverslip and immediately wipe off residual VALAP from the steel surface.

description: Asymmetric cell division (ACD) is an essential mechanism that generates cell diversity, drives tissue repair and therefore maintains tissue homeostasis (Knoblich, 2010). For example, many cell types, including stem cells, are characterized by the asymmetric distribution of specific mRNAs or proteins between daughter cells. This biased delivery is essential for specific fate acquisition (Homem and Knoblich, 2012; Gallaud et al., 2017). Drosophila larval neural stem cells (NSCs) (also known as neuroblasts, NBs) display an asymmetric positioning of the division furrow. Their division generates a large self-renewing NSC and a smaller ganglion mother cell (GMC) committed to differentiation (Thomas et al., 2021; Connell et al., 2011; Albertson and Doe, 2003). This cell size difference, together with the available transgenic lines, mutants, and numerous tools available in Drosophila melanogaster, make NSCs a valuable model to study the molecular mechanisms of asymmetric cell division. Each Drosophila larval brain explant can be kept alive for several hours for imaging experiments and contain an average of 100 NSCs that exhibit rapid cell cycles (45–60 min). Here we describe a protocol to perform centrosome laser-ablation of mitotic NCSs and to investigate daughter cell size asymmetry following cytokinesis. This protocol could be adapted to monitor cytoskeleton dynamics in other tissues.
